newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S ANC TO LAUNCH MILITARY VETERANS' GROUP.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S ANC TO LAUNCH MILITARY VETERANS' GROUP.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress, not forgetting its soldiers from the liberation struggle although their role has gone, is to set up a veterans' association this weekend to honour them.
The association will be formed at a conference to mark the 36th anniversary of the launch of the ANC's military wing, Umkhonto we Sizwe (MK, Spear of the Nation) on December 16.
The conference will be opened by the first commander of MK, President Nelson Mandela.

Long criticised for not taking care of their former combatants in the new South Africa, the ANC's Veterans' Association will address the problems some now face -- such as homelessness, unemployment and getting disability grants.

Former veteran Maxwell Sisulu said: "This is to ensure that veterans of the struggle do benefit. In most countries, it is the responsibility of the state to take care of their veterans. This was recognised in our interim constitution as well."
Veteran and chairman of the Preparatory Committee, Isaac Mokapo said: "We want to build a home for former cadres so that we can keep the name and the history of the organisation alive."
According to official figures, there were 28,000 MK cadres before the organisation disbanded on the eve of South Africa's historic democratic elections on April 26, 1994.
Of these, 11,870 have been formally integrated into the new South African National Defence force with the rest demobilised.
